summary: IPv6 uses a fixed 40-byte header with 128-bit addresses. It drops the header checksum and in-network fragmentation and moves optional features into extension headers, making forwarding simpler.

sections.heading: Fields
bullets: Version (4 bits): 6.
Traffic Class (8): DSCP and ECN.
Flow Label (20): lets routers keep packets of one flow together (e.g. for load balancing).
Payload Length (16): bytes after the 40-byte header, including extension headers.
Next Header (8): the next header type (6 TCP, 17 UDP, 58 ICMPv6, or an extension header).
Hop Limit (8): replaces TTL.
Source and Destination: 128 bits each.

sections.heading: Differences from IPv4
bullets: Fixed 40-byte header: faster to parse in hardware.
No header checksum: link layer and transport checksums protect data; saves per-hop recomputation.
Routers never fragment; only the source does, using the Fragment extension header.
No IPv4-style options; extensions chain via Next Header.
UDP checksum becomes mandatory.
No broadcast; multicast and anycast replace it.

sections.heading: Extension headers
sections.body: Optional headers sit between the base header and the upper-layer payload. RFC 8200 recommends this order: Hop-by-Hop Options, Destination Options (for intermediate destinations), Routing, Fragment, Authentication, ESP, Destination Options (final), then the upper-layer header. Each should appear at most once (Destination Options at most twice).
bullets: Only Hop-by-Hop Options must be processed by every router.
Fragment header: 13-bit offset in 8-byte units, M flag, 32-bit Identification.
Everything up to the upper-layer header must be in the first fragment.

sections.heading: MTU rules
sections.body: Every IPv6 link must support an MTU of at least 1280 bytes. Hosts should use Path MTU Discovery (RFC 8201); routers drop oversized packets and return ICMPv6 Packet Too Big.
Eight groups of four hex digits, with leading zeros droppable and one run of zero groups replaced by `::`. Example: 2001:0db8:0000:0000:0000:0000:0000:0001 is 2001:db8::1.
bullets: ::1 loopback.
fe80::/10 link-local.
fc00::/7 unique local (private).
2000::/3 global unicast.
ff00::/8 multicast.

sections.body: A host builds a link-local address, learns the prefix from Router Advertisements, and forms its own global address (RFC 4862), using ICMPv6 Neighbor Discovery in place of ARP and parts of DHCP.

bullets: Dual stack: run both protocols.
Tunnelling (6in4, 6rd).
NAT64/DNS64: IPv6-only clients reach IPv4 servers.

sections.body: Link-layer CRCs catch most bit errors and transport protocols checksum the data plus a pseudo-header of the addresses, so an IP header checksum duplicates work and costs time at every hop.

takeaways: Fixed 40-byte header, 128-bit addresses, Hop Limit instead of TTL.
No header checksum and no router fragmentation.
Extension headers chain through Next Header in a recommended order.
Minimum MTU is 1280; Path MTU Discovery is essential.

references.label: RFC 8201: Path MTU Discovery for IPv6
